entities.summary: Matteo dal Nasaro Veronese, also known as Matteo dal Nasaro of Verona, was an Italian sculptor of the late Renaissance period, born in Verona, Italy around 1490, and died in 1548. He was trained by the renowned sculptor Michelangelo, and his works, including the iconic 'St. James' in Verona's Castelvecchio Museum, showcase his mastery of classical techniques and emotional depth. Matteo's contributions to the development of Mannerism and his collaboration with artists such as Titian and Tintoretto demonstrate his significance in the cultural landscape of 16th-century Italy. His legacy can be seen in the works of later generations of Italian artists, including Raphael and Caravaggio, who were influenced by his innovative style and technical skill. As a testament to his enduring impact, Matteo's 'St. James' continues to inspire artists and art lovers to this day, standing as a powerful symbol of faith and devotion in the heart of Verona's historic city center.
